teddyStatementVerdict: QUALIFIED — confirmed for reads and for the bulk, contradicted for writes and for precisely the gaps he wants closed. CONFIRMED HALF: the metadata mechanism really is as cheap as he says, and I verified it end to end. safeWrite fetches and hard-resets to origin/main before re-running its mutation (teamRepo.ts:15, :125-126), refreshClone runs per team (sync.ts:147), and every people-file writer re-serializes the PARSED document (install.ts:139, uninstall.ts:106, sync.ts:392, :404, team.ts:408/:418), so a committed field propagates to every other machine on its next sync with zero sync code. personSchema (schema.ts:64), teamSchema.projects (:48), configSchema (:105) and the receipt (receipt.ts, passthrough at every level, schema_version z.literal(1) at :51) are all passthrough, so additions are free and a version bump is never the mechanism. Concretely: 166 of 196 rows are SIMPLE, and 53 of the 62 SIMPLE CLI-side rows need NO new field anywhere — they are Result fields, exports, flags, verb payloads and library reads. That is genuinely 'low cost by updating the metadata'. CONTRADICTED HALF, three ways. (1) 'More intelligent sync' is the wrong lever, and the document's own section 2 says so: sync has no writer for anything new, no names payload and no notion of a machine. Only seven rows spend a new-field allowance at all, and of the three config.json ones, two are refused on the MERITS rather than on price — CP-D1 ('it should not be built at all': team.json already carries `name`, written from the same string at team.ts:525 and published as the README heading) and MC-01 (no field and no flag recommended; the app sets the child's cwd, which lib.rs already does). (2) The gaps that actually block 'full canvas functionality' are not metadata gaps. Of the twelve FRAME_FEATURES flags (frames.ts:39-42), metadata plus sync buys at most `roles` and `projectMembers`. favorites/follow need a ledger sentence retiring D38; perCase/liftOnCards/runEvalInApp need Ajay to amend a standing §12 prohibition; disablePerMachine needs a mechanism that does not exist, because placement IS loading; `progress` has no emitter and the source says so in as many words (frames.ts:22-23, 'Reserved: no verb emits progress yet'); lastSeen/installScope/inviteScoping are refused or deferred. Ten of twelve are decisions, permissions or absent mechanisms — not one is a metadata field. (3) 'Monorepo structure' is not the constraint he thinks it is. The team-repo schema is closed by CODE, not by layout: guard.ts:50 routes every team.json change through guardTeam, which at guard.ts:150-156 admits exactly three shapes and throws. No restructuring and no smarter sync moves that line; it takes Ryan reopening a table the spec calls closed, which is why AC-07, CP-14, TJ-02 and TJ-12 are all refused and why S7ab has to be gated. NET: 'nearly everything is low cost' is true of the bulk and false of the residual he is actually asking about — the greyed controls on the canvas. The M7 document is honest about this in section 0.1 and section 6.1, which are its strongest passages; the premise it is answering is not. The one correction I would make to the document's own framing: it should state plainly that Teddy's gap-cost reading is right about the 166 SIMPLE rows and wrong about the causal claim, rather than opening with 'Not on its own', which reads as a scoping quibble instead of the substantive disagreement it is.
